name: Sulfuric acid (concentrated)
context: A strong Brønsted acid; only hot and concentrated does it also act as an oxidant.
typicalUses: Acid catalyst (esterification, dehydration of alcohols)
With HNO₃: generates NO₂⁺ for nitration
Drying/dehydrating agent
chemoselectivity: Dilute H₂SO₄ is just a strong acid: Zn gives H₂, and Cu does not react
pitfalls: Hot and concentrated, it oxidises Cu to CuSO₄ (giving SO₂) and HBr/HI to Br₂/I₂
Dilution is strongly exothermic: add acid to water

name: Trifluoroacetic acid
typicalUses: Removal of Boc and tert-butyl ester protecting groups
Cleavage of peptides from resin
chemoselectivity: Strong enough to remove Boc (via the tert-butyl cation) but leaves methyl esters and Cbz intact
pitfalls: Volatile (b.p. 72 °C), so it is easily evaporated after deprotection; the amine is left as its TFA salt

name: p-Toluenesulfonic acid
typicalUses: Acetal formation with a Dean–Stark trap
Fischer esterification
Dehydration of alcohols
chemoselectivity: A strong acid that dissolves in organic solvents; the conjugate base is non-nucleophilic
pitfalls: Usually sold as the monohydrate, which brings water into the reaction

name: Hydrochloric acid
typicalUses: Strong acid for workups and hydrolyses
Converts tertiary alcohols to tertiary chlorides (SN1)
chemoselectivity: Cl⁻ is a modest nucleophile: primary alcohols react only slowly without ZnCl₂ (Lucas reagent)
pitfalls: A non-oxidising acid: it does not dissolve Cu or Ag

name: Boron trifluoride etherate
typicalUses: Activates epoxides, carbonyls and acetals towards nucleophiles
Catalyses Mukaiyama aldol and other C–C bond formations
chemoselectivity: A strong, oxophilic Lewis acid; BF₃ is supplied complexed to diethyl ether so it can be handled as a liquid
pitfalls: Hydrolyses in moist air, fuming (giving HF-containing species)

name: Aluminium chloride
typicalUses: Friedel–Crafts alkylation and acylation
chemoselectivity: Alkylation: carbocations rearrange and the product is more reactive (polyalkylation)
Acylation: no rearrangement, and the product ketone is deactivated so it stops at monoacylation
Strongly deactivated rings (nitrobenzene) do not react
pitfalls: Acylation needs a full equivalent of AlCl₃, because the product ketone binds it
Reacts violently with water, releasing HCl

name: Titanium(IV) chloride
typicalUses: Mukaiyama aldol reaction
Chelation-controlled additions to α- or β-alkoxy carbonyls
chemoselectivity: Can chelate two oxygens at once, which locks the conformation and controls diastereoselectivity
pitfalls: Fumes in air (hydrolysis to TiO₂ + HCl)
With Zn or LiAlH₄ it forms low-valent titanium for McMurry coupling

name: Zinc chloride
typicalUses: Lucas reagent (with conc. HCl): distinguishes 1°, 2° and 3° alcohols
Catalyst for Fischer indole synthesis
chemoselectivity: A mild Lewis acid; in the Lucas test, tertiary alcohols turn cloudy at once, secondary within minutes, primary not at room temperature

name: Iron(III) bromide
typicalUses: Catalyst for electrophilic aromatic bromination (with Br₂)
chemoselectivity: Polarises Br–Br to make a 'Br⁺' equivalent; often generated in situ from Fe and Br₂
pitfalls: Not needed for strongly activated rings (phenol, aniline), which brominate without it

name: Boron tribromide
typicalUses: Cleavage of methyl ethers (especially aryl methyl ethers) to alcohols/phenols
chemoselectivity: Coordinates the ether oxygen, then bromide attacks the methyl group
pitfalls: Reacts violently with water and alcohols

name: Silver nitrate
typicalUses: Test for halide ions (AgCl white, AgBr cream, AgI yellow)
Promotes SN1 reactions of alkyl halides by removing the halide
chemoselectivity: Ag⁺ binds halides strongly; the precipitates' solubility in NH₃(aq) distinguishes them (AgCl dissolves, AgI does not)
pitfalls: Ag⁺ is also a mild oxidant (Tollens' reagent)
